Both work, no duplicates created. Open the two versions below. In **each**, do the same thing: paste a link that's **already saved** and press **Save** — use the NASA page:
```
https://nasa.gov/webb
```

- **Option A — a heads-up, then jump to it:** http://maker:4001/dup-a.html
  You'll get a short "you already saved this" notice, and the app scrolls to and highlights the existing bookmark. From there you can press **Update it** (or its Edit button) to change it.

- **Option B — go straight to updating it:** http://maker:4001/dup-b.html
  It skips the notice and immediately opens that bookmark's edit screen, pre-filled, so you can update and Save right away.

Both refuse to create a second copy either way.

One assumption I'd like you to check: I treat a link as "already saved" when it's **the same address ignoring small differences** like `http` vs `https`, a leading `www.`, or a trailing `/` — so `nasa.gov/webb` and `https://www.nasa.gov/webb/` count as the same bookmark. Please tell me if that matches your sense of "the same link."

**After trying both, tell me which duplicate behaviour you prefer — and whether that "same link" rule is right.**
